Pleased to announce https://github.com/basisresearch/lean.py, a library for bidirectional interop between Lean 4 and Python. In particular it supports /effortless/ bindings for calling Lean from Python, and calling Python from Lean

  • For calling Lean from Python workflows, @[python "name"] in lean exports a definition for use in python with automatic marshalling of arguments and return values, then in Python, LeanLibrary.from_lake(...) loads the module and extracts the exported symbols and exposes them to python.

  • For calling Python from Lean workflows, Lean code can call into Python via an opaque Py type backed by dlopen/CPython.

There's also a kernel facade (wrapping https://github.com/leanprover/Pantograph) that lets Python drive Lean's
type-checker, elaborator, and tactic engine without spawning a subprocess.

A few examples of this library that might be interesting to people here:

- by sympy / by knuckle tactics: illustrate Lean tactics that are implemented in Python using standard python libraries - each sends the goal's Expr tree to Python via Py.ofLeanObj, convert it to a SymPy expression (or Z3 formula), check validity, and close the goal with an oracle axiom. (the docs contain a step by step walkthrough of this pipeline https://basisresearch.github.io/lean.py/examples/04_sympy_tactic.html)

- Typed numpy: A Lean library that wraps numpy with phantom-typed NDArray dt shape — array shapes and dtypes are checked at compile time by Lean. You get the python ecosystem, but a richer type system exploiting Lean's dependent types.

Docs (with walkthroughs of each example): https://basisresearch.github.io/lean.py
Discussion for this project should continue at #lean4 > Discussion for `lean.py`.

Pleased to announce that https://github.com/BasisResearch/lean.py now has a drop-in z3 shim (lean_py.z3). You write can propositions in the z3py vocabulary, Lean's tactic engine (grind, omega, decide, simp, etc.) does the proving, and the kernel checks the result. 

 from lean_py.z3 import *

 x, y = Ints('x y')
 prove(Implies(And(x > 0, y > 0), x + y > 0))  # proved

Also, now based on user feedback, install should be just one command (plus https://github.com/leanprover/elan on PATH):

  uv pip install "lean_py @ git+https://github.com/BasisResearch/lean.py"

This sets up a managed Lake project and caches it on first run, so there's no manual lakefile to setup (unless you want to).

The API tries to adhere to z3py as closely as possible, covering booleans, integers, reals, naturals, bit-vectors, arrays, sets, strings, regex, floating point, uninterpreted sorts and functions, quantifiers, recursive functions, algebraic datatypes, pseudo-boolean constraints, and SMT-LIB2 parsing. Datatypes compile to real Lean inductives, so you get constructor injectivity, disjointness, and exhaustive case analysis from the kernel.

It does deviate where the backend requires it. Obviously, Lean is a theorem prover rather than an SMT solver, so Solver.check() returns unsat or unknown, never sat, and model extraction is not supported.

One fun bit: z3py has a Tactic class (Tactic("simplify"), Then(t1, t2), OrElse(...)) for Z3's internal tactic combinators. In lean_py.z3 these just dispatch to Lean's tactic engine directly, so Tactic("omega") sends omega to Lean, and you can pass any valid tactic string, e.g. Tactic("intro x; cases x <;> simp").

Full guide: https://basisresearch.github.io/lean.py/z3py-guide.html
